summary: ASOS reported pre-tax losses of almost £300m in the year to 3 September 2023, up from £31m the previous year, as it faces competition from Shein, economic headwinds, and changing consumer habits. Experts like Rick Smith of Forbes Burton say its free-returns model and huge catalogue are weak points, while social media shopping pulls young buyers away. The company is carrying £648.5m of net debt and plans to spend £30m more on marketing and go "back to fashion".
one_line: ASOS's pre-tax losses ballooned to almost £300m amid debt, costly free returns, shifting shopper habits and competition from Shein.
key_facts: ASOS's pre-tax losses reached almost £300m in the year to 3 September 2023, compared with £31m the previous year, according to results published on 1 November.
ASOS launched in 2000; the name originally stood for As Seen On Screen, and it first sold imitations of clothing worn by celebrities.
ASOS now offers 850 affordable to mid-range high-street brands and ships to 196 countries.
The retailer cut its stock by 30 per cent after being hit by wet weather in July and August.
Net debt including leases is £648.5m, up from £533m the year before.
Analysts say ASOS may need to raise quick cash, potentially through the rumoured sale of Topshop, which it acquired when the Arcadia Group went bust in 2021.
Rick Smith of Forbes Burton says ASOS's large number of free returns leads to slim profit margins and leaves it exposed in tough economic conditions.
Smith says customers increasingly want a more tailored service, and suggests curated collections and recommendations based on user input.
Young people increasingly buy from retailers on Instagram and TikTok or directly from brands ASOS stocks, such as Pull and Bear, Stüssy and Bershka.
CEO José Antonio Ramos Calamonte said ASOS made "good progress" in "a very challenging environment".
ASOS plans to spend £30m more on marketing and go "back to fashion" with its products.
Shein, valued at around £53bn, reportedly acquired Missguided; in 2022 it was the most-googled fashion brand in the world with reported revenue of £18.9bn.
